how: Mushrif Range Shooting runs one-hour archery lessons with equipment included in Mushrif Park, and Dubai Archers Club (D'Archers) is a volunteer-run club active for 20+ years.
Dubai Dingoes and other clubs played in the AFL Middle East nines league (since 2008/09) at Dubai Sports City, but current club activity was not confirmed.
Dubai is flat desert and coast with no big walls; the nearest big rock is in the Hajar Mountains of Ras Al Khaimah and Oman's Musandam, about 1.5-2 hours away.
Adventure Zone indoor skate parks in Dubai malls (Galleria, Times Square Centre) have a BMX area on timed passes; no outdoor BMX track was confirmed.
No bobsleigh or skeleton track exists in the UAE; the climate is hot desert.
Rock Republic in Dubai Investment Park is a Walltopia-built bouldering centre with 150+ routes up to 4.5 m with mats, and Mountain Extreme lists 129 bouldering problems with beginner courses.
Buzkashi is a Central Asian horseback sport tied to Afghanistan; no UAE equivalent club exists in Dubai.
Camel racing is a spectator sport at Nad Al Sheba / Al Marmoom tracks on the Dubai outskirts (season roughly October to April); racing itself is for owners with robot jockeys.
Afro-Ritmo Capoeira runs adult and children's classes in Jumeirah Lake Towers, and Nacao Capoeira Dubai has also run classes in the city.

Dubai Offshore Sailing Club runs RYA dinghy courses and has Optimist, Laser, Pico and open dinghy fleets off Umm Suqeim beach.
Elephant polo needs working elephants (Nepal, Thailand, India); there are none in Dubai.
Dubai Fencing Club, founded in 2002 by coach Mihail Kouzev, trains foil, epee and sabre fencers; it met at the Quay Health Club, Mina A'Salam, in older reports.
Dubai Celts GAA (formed 1995) fields men's, ladies' and juvenile Gaelic football, hurling and camogie and runs the annual Dubai Duty Free Gulf Gaelic Games.
Dubai Polo & Equestrian Club and Emirates Equestrian Centre give riding lessons from beginner to advanced, with lessons listed from about Dhs240.
The Dubai Mall's Olympic-sized rink hosts Emirates Ice Hockey League games, and the UAE Ice Hockey Association runs the national league and teams.

how: The Dubai Mall has an Olympic-sized ice rink used for public skating sessions and Emirates Ice Hockey League games.

how: Mountain Extreme lists about 125 top-rope routes and 14 auto-belays with beginner courses for juniors and adults, and other Dubai gyms offer auto-belay walls.
The Warrior Academy (Al Quoz) lists judo alongside taekwondo, karate and jiu-jitsu, but is described as child-focused, so adult judo is unconfirmed.
NISAA Fitness hosts ladies-only netball sessions listed on Meetup.
Padel is widely played in Dubai, with Meetup groups such as Padel Nation running weekly social nights with rackets and balls included.
Picklers in Al Quoz is an indoor club with six enclosed climate-controlled pickleball courts, and other venues such as PickleTurf at Port Rashid also take court bookings.
Dubai Polo & Equestrian Club in Arabian Ranches has a polo academy and riding school with beginner polo lessons.
Dubai Exiles RFC (founded 1966) at The Sevens on Al Ain Road runs mini, youth, senior men's and women's rugby plus social touch rugby for adults, and welcomes newcomers.
XDubai Skatepark at Kite Beach is a 3,100 sq m park with a day pass of about AED 75, and free public parks exist at Al Mamzar, The Block (d3), Business Bay and elsewhere.
Ski jumping needs a large outdoor hill with natural snow; Ski Dubai is too small and has no jump; nearest hills are in Europe.
Ski Dubai inside Mall of the Emirates has a 85 m high indoor mountain with five runs, a chairlift and a tow lift for skiers and snowboarders, with lessons and rental on site.
WTTU Moo Duk Taekwondo (DIFC, Sports City, Al Barari), The Warrior Academy and The Ballet Centre Dubai teach taekwondo from toddlers to adults.
Dubai has a long-running ultimate community (Dubai Ultimate Players Association, United Arabian Ultimate) that hosted the 2015 World Championships of Beach Ultimate and plays recreational sessions.

Dubai Silicon Oasis Community Farm rents residents roughly 8x4 ft irrigated plots for the September-May growing season, and Wasl Oasis II in Muhaisnah has a resident organic allotment; these are resident-only schemes.
Overnight camping in Dubai emirate is restricted to Dubai Municipality-permitted areas (e.g. Wadi Al Amerdi, Al Warqa, Al Khawaneej), and Al Qudra camping has been officially banned in places.
After winter rains wild edible and medicinal plants such as humaid (sorrel) grow in desert and wadis and are traditionally gathered; no organised foraging walks were found.
venue: Desert and wadi areas of Dubai

how: Hundreds of geocaches are hidden in Dubai parks (including Safa Park) and desert areas, found with GPS apps via geocaching.com.
Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary at the head of Dubai Creek has free public bird hides with flamingos; organised guided walks were not confirmed.
Meetup groups (Alpine Trekkers, AFT Mountain Adventures) run weekly hikes in the Hajar Mountains, with Hatta about 1.5 hours from the centre; Dubai itself is flat desert and coast.
Mushrif National Park has a roughly 50 km colour-coded mountain bike track (green beginner to black expert); a roundup also lists bike rental at Al Qudra and club rides at District One.
Dubai Sports World runs map-and-control-point orienteering sessions at beginner to advanced levels inside its indoor complex; no outdoor orienteering club was found.
The Dubai metro area is flat desert and coast with no crags; the nearest outdoor climbing is in the Hajar Mountains near Hatta and Ras Al Khaimah, about 1.5 hours away.
Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary has three free public bird hides; its species list includes osprey, Eurasian marsh harrier and spotted eagle among flamingos and waders.

Dubai Astronomy Group runs public stargazing nights at Al Qudra desert (about an hour from the centre, entry free to independent visitors) and the Al Thuraya Astronomy Centre in Mushrif Park offers telescopes.
venue: Al Thuraya Astronomy Centre, Mushrif Park

how: Mirdif Milers, a free club open to all abilities, meets every Monday evening at the main gate of Mushrif Park and runs the park's paths; dedicated desert trail groups meet at Al Qudra, beyond the metro radius.

Greenoponics, a Dubai company, sets up soil-less home and office growing systems, while commercial vertical farms such as Badia Farms and UNS Farms operate in Al Quoz; open hobbyist workshops are not confirmed.
Sky Hub Remote Control Club runs a model aircraft flying field at Al Lisaili and has hosted UAE RC championships; the evidence is for radio-controlled rather than control-line flying.
Dubai Paddle Club is a dragon boat crew based at Dubai Offshore Sailing Club, and Dubai Dolphins, Barracuda and Move One Dubai Sea Dragons also paddle, under the UAE Dragon Boat Association.
Deep-sea fishing charters depart Dubai Marina twice daily on 4-hour trips with tackle and bait included (about AED 312 each on Platinum List).
Natfreediver runs AIDA freediving trial classes and AIDA 2/3 courses at Wellfit Meydan (pool) and Deep Dive Dubai (deep pool), with gear rental.
Guided Dubai kayak tours (e.g. Hydro Water Sports at Royal Central The Palm) pass small mangrove stands; dedicated mangrove kayaking is mainly in Abu Dhabi.
Sunrise hot air balloon flights over the Dubai desert run daily from October to May.
Guided and rental kayak tours run along the Dubai coast and Marina, for example from Hydro Water Sports at Royal Central The Palm.
Dubai Offshore Sailing Club has IRC-rated keelboat racing fleets, RYA cruising and yacht courses and monthly cruising rallies in UAE waters from October to April.
Kite Beach in Jumeirah is a free public beach where kites are flown, and the International Kite Festival has been held on the Jumeirah 3 beachfront.
Kitesurfing.ae teaches kitesurfing from Dubai's beaches with discovery courses, 10-hour beginner courses and hourly lessons plus equipment rental.
SeaYou Watersport Center on Palm Jumeirah rents pedalos alongside kayaks, SUP and sailboats; pedal boats are also hired at Zabeel Park and Al Barsha Pond Park.
The Emirates Aerosport Federation holds RC aircraft competitions at Zabeel Park and the SkyHub RC flying field at Al Lisaili; no open Dubai club was confirmed.
Recreational drones can be flown legally after registration and a hobbyist certificate from an authorised centre such as Sanad Academy, which offers a three-hour beginner course.

Monty's Rowing School offers coastal rowing lessons and Dubai Creek sessions for beginners, based at a beach club on the Palm Jumeirah (listing from 2014, so current availability should be confirmed).
Dubai Offshore Sailing Club (est. 1974) is an RYA Training Centre on Jumeirah Beach Road with keelboat and dinghy racing fleets, cruising rallies and sailing courses.

PADI centres such as Bermuda Diving Center (Jumeirah 3), Scuba Shade and ScubaDive.ae run try-dives from about AED 250-580 and Open Water courses (around AED 2,500) in the Gulf, plus a pool at Deep Dive Dubai.
Atlantis Aquaventure offers a guided snorkel in the Lost Chambers aquarium lagoon; natural reefs are a roughly two-hour trip to Fujairah or Dibba, and local Gulf visibility is low.
venue: Atlantis The Palm, Ultimate Snorkel Experience

how: IGNITE Sport Services rents stand-up paddleboards on Palm Jumeirah by the hour (about AED 95) with a short beginner lesson, paddle and life vest included.
Paddleboard yoga has been run by Sup Yoga Dubai at beach hotels and Super SUP Fit in pools; listings are dated and current schedules are unconfirmed.
Wild Wadi water park has FlowRider-style standing-wave surf simulators (Wipeout and Riptide).
Surf House Dubai offers surf and paddleboard lessons on the small Gulf swell, while Dubai's main wave sports are kitesurfing at Kite Beach; real ocean surf waves are rare.
Boat wakeboarding operators such as Wake Surf Dubai and CrazyWake run beginner and small-group sessions from Jumeirah Fishing Harbour and Dubai Harbour Marina.
Operators such as Blue Safari Water Sports (Palm Jumeirah) and CharterClick (Dubai Marina) offer boat-towed water skiing for beginners with skis and life jackets supplied.
SeaYou offers windsurfing and stand-up paddle lessons and tours from its Palm Jumeirah watersports centre.

Courtyard Playhouse is an independent theatre and performing-arts training centre running improv and acting workshops for adults and children; Dubai Drama Group (founded 1984) stages community theatre with workshops.
Tempo Dance Academy's JLT Latin programme lists tango among its courses; no dedicated Argentine tango milonga was confirmed.
The Dubai Pipe Band, a volunteer band of about 13 pipers and drummers, performs in Dubai and lists a contact for enquiries; whether it teaches beginners was not confirmed.
The Ballet Centre Dubai (Motor City, Jumeirah), The National Ballet Studio (Jumeirah Islands) and Melodica Music Academy teach ballet to adults and children, many with trial classes.
Laasya Performing Arts in Jebel Ali Village teaches Bharatanatyam and Kathak to children and adults and performs at Global Village.
Tempo Dance Center in Jumeirah Lake Towers lists break dance lessons, and Red Bull BC One regional events have run in Dubai.
Studio Republik, Pole Fit Dubai and TRIX DXB (International City) teach aerial silks, hoop and hammock classes.
One Day Choir Dubai runs no-audition single-day choir sessions, and Dubai Camerata Singers is a multicultural community choir founded in 2017.
The National Youth Orchestra - Dubai has around 120 resident musicians aged 5-18; the new Dubai Orchestra foundation was approved in 2025, but no open adult amateur orchestra was found.
Dancemania DJ & Music Production studio in Al Safa runs one-to-one and group DJ courses for beginners and advanced students.
Prime Symphony Music Centre, Melodica Music Academy, SOPM and Dubai Music School (about AED 250 per hour) offer guitar lessons.
Private harp tutors (including Celtic harp, in person in Jumeirah Lake Towers and online) are listed in Dubai on MyPrivateTutor.
Courtyard Playhouse in Al Quoz is a dedicated improv theatre running workshops for adults, teens and kids with free trial classes.
The Ballet Centre in Motor City, a children's dance school, lists Irish dance among its classes; no adult or dedicated Irish dance school was found.
Laasya Performing Arts in Jebel Ali Village teaches Kathak and Bharatanatyam with trained instructors.

Lion dance is performed at Chinese New Year events and venues (Expo City, Dubai Parks, Hakkasan at Atlantis, Ibn Battuta Mall) by visiting or hired troupes; no resident practice group or class was found.
venue: Expo City Dubai (Chinese New Year parade)

how: Close-up magicians such as a Umm Suqeim-based professional and several others teach sleight-of-hand lessons in person across Dubai, and a Dubai magician runs an online magic academy.
Dancemania Music Studio in Al Safa runs DJ and music production courses, and SAWT Music Academy offers production courses in English and Arabic.
Melodica Music Academy (JLT, Town Square), Prime Symphony Music Centre (Academic City), SOPM (Dubai Investment Park) and others give private piano lessons for all ages.
Studio Republik and Pole Fit Dubai Aerial Arts Academy (Dubai Marina) run pole fitness classes for adults.
VR DanceWorld (Business Bay), MOOVnation (JLT), James & Alex Dance Studio (Media City) and Tempo Dance Academy run beginner salsa and bachata classes with social dancing.
Sitar tutors in Dubai (for example in Dubai Silicon Oasis and Palm Jumeirah) teach in person and online, and an Indian classical music teacher ran sitar classes in Al Bastakiya.

Dubomedy's arts school and the 5-week Comedy Kix beginner workshop (ending in a live set) teach stand-up, and Dubai has regular English-language comedy nights; content is subject to UAE media-content rules.
Lindy Hop Dubai ran free beginner swing sessions at a JBR hotel bar according to a 2015 listing; current activity is unconfirmed.
venue: Lindy Hop Dubai (Speakeasy Bar, Ramada Plaza)

how: Tharangini Music Centre in Al Nahda is listed for tabla and other Indian music and dance classes; no operator page was opened.
Shoten Taiko Drummers, founded in Dubai in 2014 as the Middle East's first taiko group, perform at events; open classes are not confirmed.
The Ballet Centre in Motor City and Dance For You in Garhoud list tap dance classes among their dance programmes.
Chinese opera is staged in Dubai only as visiting-company performances and festival galas (Dubai Opera Chinese New Year gala), with no local Teochew troupe found.
SAE University College Dubai teaches animation (bachelor programmes plus beginner and advanced animation short courses and creative camps).

Tashkeel has run introductory bookbinding workshops (accordion, single signature, Japanese stab binding) at Dubai Design District and Emirates Towers, and operates a makerspace at Alserkal Avenue; sessions are occasional.
Studio Kinza (Al Quoz), Resin Art Hub (Al Garhoud) and La Plume Candles run candle-making workshops of 1.5-2.5 hours, listed from AED 180.
Chinese calligraphy in Dubai appears mainly as event performances and children's writing sessions via tutor directories, with no dedicated adult class confirmed.

Tashkeel has a fully equipped darkroom and has run courses developing and printing black-and-white film, and Analog The Room is a Dubai analog photography lab offering film development workshops.
SAE Institute Dubai (Knowledge Park) offers a film diploma, BazAct blends acting with short-film making, and Skilldeer lists filmmaking classes.
Craft Land in Jumeirah teaches hand embroidery alongside sewing and quilting, and beginner courses (intro class in Jebel Ali, Town Centre Jumeirah) are listed.

The Ohara School of Ikebana UAE branch has taught in Dubai since 2014, with regular workshops open to outsiders including an annual cherry-blossom class, and Ikebana International has a Dubai chapter.
Tashkeel runs multi-session Jewellery Manufacturing Basics workshops (wax carving, sawing, filing, soldering), and The Jewel Teller at Alserkal Avenue has offered goldsmith-led metal pendant courses.
Kintsugi workshops appear as one-off events in Dubai, such as the Dubai Watch Week masterclass run by a Dubai coach-artist and a free 2017 session at Dubai Design District.
Solandis Crochet in Al Qusais teaches private beginner crochet classes (about AED 345).
Fuse DXB runs a private DIY leather jewellery workshop in Arabian Ranches listed through Skilldeer; no dedicated leatherwork studio was confirmed.
The Jamjar at Alserkal Avenue runs figure drawing workshops and Meraki Art and Design Studio lists a charcoal course; nude-model sessions are limited by UAE public-decency rules.
Tashkeel Nad Al Sheba has a dedicated Printmaking Studio and Risograph digital printing studio; lithography as a specific technique is not itemised on its pages.
Tashkeel runs weekly 'Drop-in & Knot' macrame weekend workshops led by a mentor, alongside other drop-in craft sessions.
The Palette Art in Al Barsha and Dubai International Art Centre run painting classes including oil.
Paper-folding workshops run at Studio13 (Alserkal Avenue) and Helio Studio (Al Quoz), and Tashkeel and Dubai Design Week have hosted origami sessions.
Oo La Lab in Dubai Design District runs one-hour introductory scent-blending sessions from AED 320 with no experience needed, and Grasse Institute of Perfumery offers technical courses.
Gulf Photo Plus at Alserkal Avenue runs workshops and photo walks, and Moutasem Academy, The Photography Institute and SAE Dubai teach digital photography courses.
Maison Terrae, OKA Ceramics and Yadawei Ceramic Studio in Al Quoz teach hand-building alongside wheel work, with beginner sessions from about AED 210.
Several Al Quoz studios (Maison Terrae, The Mud House Studio, OKA Ceramics, Yadawei) teach wheel throwing from single intro sessions of roughly AED 210-280.
Tufting Time runs guided rug-tufting sessions (from about AED 315) at Dubai Festival City Mall, Jumeirah and Town Square, where participants design and make their own rug.
The Workshop DXB, a screenprinting studio opposite Alserkal Avenue, ran a Dubai Culture screenprinting training programme, and Tashkeel has run multi-session screenprinting workshops.
The Mud House Studio in Al Quoz runs pottery classes (wheel throwing and hand-building), workshops and memberships for absolute beginners up to experienced potters.
Dubai's climate makes outdoor snow sculpture impossible; nearest snow festivals are in East Asia and Europe.
Licensed tattoo studios such as Dubai Hills Tattoo and Tattoo Lovers Studio operate in Dubai (a licence is required), but no public course or apprenticeship for becoming a tattoo artist was found.
Urban Sketchers Dubai, an official chapter of the international organisation, holds free on-location sketching meetups at pre-arranged spots, open to all skill levels.
Dubai International Art Centre (founded 1976, Jumeirah 1) and The Palette Art offer watercolour courses.
The Makers Society in Ras Al Khor runs woodworking trial classes (hand-saw and hand-plane basics, tools provided) plus wood-turning and kids' courses.
Origin Base in Al Quoz offers memberships and day passes with 3D printing and laser cutting training, and FabLab UAE and the Hamdan Award Fab Lab offer public access to 3D printers.
The Emirates Amateur Radio Society runs licensing training, exams and repeaters for the UAE from Sharjah, roughly 25-30 km from central Dubai.

Dubai Police runs an annual Capture the Flag contest (2025 prize pool AED 223,000, online qualifiers and in-person finals) and universities host CTFs; these are event-based rather than a standing club.
FabLab UAE lists CNC milling alongside 3D printing and laser cutting with staff training, and Origin Base has wood and metal shops for members.
AI Tinkerers Dubai holds screened in-person builder meetups, and CodersHQ is a Dubai hub for developer meetups, talks and hackathons.
Origin Base, a makerspace in Al Quoz, includes an electronics lab alongside other shops for members; the 2017-verified listing may be dated.
SAE University College Dubai runs games degrees and game-developer short courses, and Futurise lists game design and app-development courses; dedicated game jams were not confirmed.
AI Tinkerers Dubai runs in-person hackathons and demo days (a Global Hackathon in September 2026), and events such as AngelHack Dubai and Falak.me CodeFest have also been held.
Origin Base in Al Quoz has a 100 W CO2 laser cutter with safety training for members, and FabLab UAE also lists laser cutting.
Space and Rocketry Academy UAE (SARAUAE) camps have taught NAR-approved kit rocketry to children with launches at Dubai Parks and Resorts; the coverage is from 2018-2019 and no adult club was found.

how: Star Geeks Robotics Smart Playground at Wafi City runs robotics building and programming for ages 4-12, and Pure Minds Academy teaches robotics, Python and electronics to ages 10-17 at venues including the Museum of the Future.
Short hands-on watchmaking workshops run at Jaeger-LeCoultre's Atelier d'Antoine in The Dubai Mall, and Van Cleef & Arpels' L'ECOLE at Dubai Design District teaches jewellery and watchmaking courses.

how: Sega Republic in Dubai Mall and family venues such as Black Bunny and Glitch have large arcade game floors.

Several board game groups, including Dubai Board Gamers, House Rules and Game Knights, host regular social game nights at cafes and venues across the city.

Dubai Chess and Culture Club in Al Mamzar has a 250-seat tournament hall, a chess school with training rooms and runs the annual Dubai Open and junior championships; Dubai Social Chess Club also meets.
Dubai Ladies Bridge Club (founded 1981) plays in pairs twice weekly at the Dubai International Women's Clubhouse on Jumeirah Beach Road, with partner-matching for single players.
Cosplayers gather mainly at the annual Middle East Film and Comic Con at Dubai World Trade Centre, which includes cosplay competitions and workshops.

how: The Gulf Roleplaying Community runs tabletop RPG games in the UAE, and tabletop.me, a Dubai tabletop convention held at the Concourse Convention Center in Dubai Outlet Mall, included Dungeons & Dragons sessions.
Dubai has dozens of escape rooms, including Game Over, NoWayOut in JLT, Escape Hunt at Galleria Mall and horror-themed Escape House, typically 60-minute games for 2-10 players.
Dubai has gaming cafes such as Esport Arena that host PC cafe tournaments, and the Dubai Esports and Games Festival runs competitions in titles like Valorant and League of Legends.
Dubai hosts the tabletop.me convention with live role-playing sessions and 60+ game masters, a Dubai Board Gamers group, and the Gulf Roleplaying Community; no regular live-action LARP was confirmed.

Mahjong Dubai, a Riichi (Japanese-style) mahjong group, hosts regular meetups in the city.
Battlezone on Jumeirah Road was listed as hosting card and war gamers with Warhammer 40K among the most popular games; the listing is old.
Singo Paintball is an air-conditioned indoor paintball arena in Dubai, and Battle Park and Action Park run outdoor fields with gear supplied.
Quiz & Chill runs social trivia nights in Dubai listed on Meetup.

how: Dubai International Bowling Centre in Al Mamzar has 36 lanes, and Black Bunny in Al Quoz and Glitch at Al Ghurair Centre have eight-lane alleys.

Mirzam Chocolate Makers, a bean-to-bar factory in Al Quoz, runs chocolate factory tours with moulding, tasting and coffee-and-cocoa pairing workshops.

Terra at Expo City Dubai runs a five-part novice beekeeping course (classroom, practical sessions and field trips, protective gear provided), and the Beekeepers Association UAE runs a seven-week novice course at The Sustainable City.
ICCA Dubai teaches bartending and alcohol-free mixology courses, PATH Bar School offers cocktail and spirits certification, and venues such as Time Out Market run paid cocktail masterclasses.
RAW Coffee Company roasts in Al Quoz and runs coffee training (barista and brewing courses, an Art of Cupping workshop at the roastery) but lists no dedicated roasting course.
Hotel restaurants such as Shiba at Meydan Hotel and Zhen Wei at Caesars Palace Bluewaters have run occasional two-hour dim sum classes.
Kombucha workshops have been run as one-offs, for example by chef Nida Sumar at Jossa by Alserkal in May 2023 and by Tabchilli; no regular class schedule was found.

activity: Hands-on cooking classes (pasta and other cuisines)
how: Le Gourmet at Galeries Lafayette and Culinary Boutique run hands-on cooking workshops across cuisines including pasta, sushi and dumplings.

Frying Pan Adventures runs guided multi-stop food walks through Old Dubai (spice and gold souks, Bur Dubai, creekside) and neighbourhood food tours such as Little India and Middle Eastern pilgrimage routes.
Urasenke-style tea ceremonies and matcha workshops are held in Dubai by a study group and by organisers such as IKIGAI-SHU, mostly as occasional events.
ICCA Dubai's Artisanal Coffee programme includes a full day of hands-on latte art, and City & Guilds barista skills courses run at Dubai Knowledge Park.
Zuma Dubai hosts sake dinners and tastings in its Ishigaki wine room with visiting master brewers, and Hakkasan has run sake masterclasses; alcohol is served only in licensed venues.
One-off sourdough workshops are run by home bakers and bakeries, such as a sourdough experience at The Bread Basket in Jumeirah 1.
SUSHISAMBA Dubai has run an Edomae sushi masterclass with lunch, and the Meydan Hotel's Shiba restaurant ran a dim sum and sushi class.

Hotel and venue whisky tastings and masterclasses (a Le Clos Taste of Whisky evening at Bulgari Hotel Yacht Club, Macallan pairing tastings at The St. Regis) run as ticketed events in licensed venues rather than as a standing class.
The Tasting Class has offered WSET Level 1 and 2 wine courses to the public in Dubai since 2017, alongside tasting events in hotels and restaurants.
Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary has three free public birding hides overlooking greater flamingos, stilts, egrets, avocets and migratory shorebirds at the head of Dubai Creek.
Dubai Butterfly Garden is a covered garden housing thousands of live butterflies that visitors can walk through and photograph.

Dealers and the annual Currency Fair (NGC and PMG attended) serve collectors, and Numisbing is a Dubai numismatic company; the free Dubai Coins Museum in Al Fahidi displays coins, but no membership society was found.
Comicave at Dubai Outlet Mall sells comics, manga, figures and collectibles aimed at serious collectors, with Marvel Vault at IMG Worlds of Adventure and smaller comic shops as alternatives.

The Dubai Natural History Group runs member field trips that include geology outings (Hatta copper deposits, Rainbow Valley, Buhais Geology Park) and a past fossil-hunting trip; trips are for members only.
Sneaker retail and resale is established: Youbetterfly consignment stores, Concepts (City Walk), Good Life Space (Alserkal Avenue) and Corcel (d3), plus Sole DXB and Dubai Sneaker Week events.
The Emirates Philatelic Association (founded 1996, 700+ members) is based in Dubai and organises stamp exhibitions including the Dubai 2026 World Stamp Exhibition.
Comicave at Dubai Outlet Mall stocks action figures, statues and models for collectors, with a tabletop gaming area, and Marvel Vault at IMG Worlds sells collector merchandise.
PokeMENA in Dubai Silicon Oasis sells Pokemon and graded trading cards, and BattleZone stocks Yu-Gi-Oh, Magic and Pokemon cards.
The Flip Side at Alserkal Avenue is an independent vinyl store, and Raw Music Store, Metal East Records and Cavo also sell new and used records.
Collector groups Dubai Watch Club and Emirates Watch Club hold meetups, and Dubai Watch Week is an annual collector show.

Only rare whale and whale-shark sightings off Dubai (humpback 2017, orcas 2022); no whale-watching tours found, nearest organised marine-wildlife cruises are in Musandam (Oman), roughly 3 hours by road.

The Dubai Municipality Historical Documents Centre in Al Shindagha holds historical records and treaties with researcher offices upstairs; free guided visits are offered and research requests go through the centre, with no open reading room described.
Alserkal Avenue in Al Quoz hosts about 25 contemporary art galleries and spaces such as Ayyam Gallery, Carbon 12 and Green Art Gallery, with exhibitions, talks and community events.
Bookends Dubai and several other Meetup book groups (Book Cellar, Dubai Bibliophiles, Iqraa Arabic Book Group) hold regular book club meetings in Dubai.
The Dubai Writers' Group (founded 2005) runs a critique group and sit-and-write sessions for amateur and professional writers, welcoming complete beginners.
Dubai Toastmasters Club meets twice monthly at Villa Rotana in Business Bay with prepared speeches and speech contests; no standalone adult debate league was found.

The Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding in the Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood runs Emirati cultural meals, Open House programmes, Jumeirah Mosque visits and talks for visitors and residents.
venue: Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding

how: The Jumeirah Archaeological Site (Umayyad-Abbasid town) is excavated by Dubai Culture and can be visited, but no public volunteer dig was found.
The Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding runs a Heritage Express trolley tour of the city's oldest neighbourhoods, and Frying Pan Adventures runs guided Old Dubai souk and creek walks.
venue: Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding

how: Dubai hosts several language exchange meetup groups such as The Language Society, Dubai Language & Communication Circle and Dubai Expats Social & Language Exchange.

Alliance Francaise Dubai teaches French from complete beginner to advanced (group classes, private tuition, kids and teens, DELF/DALF exam prep) at Oud Metha and Dubai Knowledge Park, plus cultural events.
Goethe-Institut Gulf Region runs German courses from A1 to C2 (standard and intensive, on-site and online) at its Dubai centre in Bur Dubai.

Eton Institute teaches Korean from beginner (A0) to advanced in group, private and live-online formats at its Dubai centre; many other institutes are listed in Dubai.

Museum of the Future on Sheikh Zayed Road is an immersive exhibition venue across five themed floors on science, technology and innovation.
Dubai Culture runs a free e-learning programme giving creatives access to thousands of LinkedIn Learning courses, alongside global MOOC platforms usable from Dubai.
Practical Philosophy Club - Dubai and PhiloLifers Dubai host philosophy discussion events listed on Meetup.
Dubai Bibliophiles Book Club hosts poetry sessions listed on Meetup; no dedicated slam series was confirmed.

No snow or sled-dog culture exists in the UAE; the nearest option is in cold-climate Europe or Asia, many hours away by air.
No glaciers exist in the UAE or nearby Gulf region; the nearest glacier trekking is in the Alps or Central Asia, many hours away by air.
Aventura Parks in Mushrif Park offers colour-graded high-rope adventure circuits with ziplines, tight ropes and wobble bridges for all levels.
